To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a method for blind SSIM estimation based on the pdfs of DCT coefficients of distorted images.
the proposed method provides a good estimation of the SSIm index for DCT based image quality assessment.

the proposed method is applicable to the encoding scheme that involves DCT quantization and the numerical results show that the relative errors of the proposed method are generally smaller than the available PSNR estimation schemes for DTC based images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new paradigm for objective quality assessment of digital images based on the SSIM index.
the development of an objective quality metric for DCT based digital images, which is capable of estimating the structural similarity between a reference image and its distorted version.
the estimation of the SS IM index in the absence of a reference image.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed blind SSIM estimation method is a promising approach for objective image quality assessment.
the proposed method can be used as a blind quality assessment method for DCT-based images.
the SSIM index is more sensitive to image distortion, and therefore, it provides better quality prediction of DCT based images compared to the peak signal to noise ration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a blind quality assessment of the digital images is possible using the proposed algorithm.
the proposed method can be used as a reliable tool for blind structural similarity estimation of the DCT based images.
the proposed blind quality assessment scheme can be used to estimate the SSIM index of the image without requiring the reference image.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SSIM metric is a useful tool for objective image quality assessment, and it is possible to estimate it in the absence of the reference image.
we can estimate the SSIM metric for a DCT encoded image using only the quantized DCT coefficient values of the distorted image.
the proposed SSIm estimation algorithm is applicable to DCT-based images and can be used for blind quality assessment.
